wording: In Whyte, Hohwy & Smith's active-inference model of masking, late P3b-like potentials and increased PFC activity were produced by the working-memory demands of self-report and vanished without report, yet simulated PFC activity on visible trials still crossed the reportability threshold. On this model, no-report results do not necessarily contradict cognitive (global-workspace or higher-order) theories.
counterevidence_limits: One computational model; shows compatibility, not that the theories are right.
verification_phrases: K13|does not necessarily contradict cognitive theories of consciousness

wording: In SIM-CONS-A's minimal threshold toy (gating + report demand), removing report cut the visible-minus-invisible PFC contrast by 60% while 84% of visible trials still exceeded the reportability threshold. K13's qualitative pattern follows from these two assumptions, so the toy shows the logic is coherent but adds no evidence about brains.
verification_phrases: n/a (simulation or framework claim; verified against execution records)

wording: Integrated information theory predicts that silencing all active neurons in the main complex leaves consciousness present (silent-brain prediction) and that disabling silent neurons can change experience (disabled-neuron prediction). Against the objection that these are untestable, Ponce de Leon & Yoshimi (2026) argue both can be tested, while noting why such theoretical disputes are hard to resolve (Lakatos).
verification_phrases: K12|showing how they can in fact be tested

wording: The Minimal Phenomenal Experience questionnaire (92 items; 1,403 usable of 3,627 responses from meditators, mostly Vipassana 43.9% and Zen 34.9%) yielded 12 factors explaining 44% of variance, including 'Pure Awareness in Dream and Sleep', 'Luminosity', 'Wakeful Presence' and 'Witness Consciousness'.
counterevidence_limits: Self-selected meditators; exploratory factor names are interpretive.
verification_phrases: K14|A solution with 12 factors explaining 44% of the total variance

wording: In SIM-CONS-A, 92 structureless items (n = 1,403) gave about 43 'factors' by the eigenvalue-above-1 rule but about 0 by parallel analysis; with 12 true factors parallel analysis recovered exactly 12 at loadings of .4 to .75, and '12 components explain 44%' corresponded to loadings near .6. K14's dimensionality is statistically plausible for data of its size; what the factors are experiences of is a separate question.
counterevidence_limits: Principal components on simulated normal items; K14 used factor analysis on real data (not re-run).
verification_phrases: n/a (simulation or framework claim; verified against execution records)

wording: 'Pure awareness' (interpretive): contemplative traditions describe consciousness without ordinary content (for example turiya in Advaita, S31), and meditators' reports of such states have a measurable structure (K14). Whether awareness without content exists as more than a reported state is a philosophical question the track does not settle.
Boundary: no theory has solved consciousness. Track Cycle A sharpened two methodological questions (report confounds, testability of IIT's silent-neuron predictions) but decided none of the theories.
